title: The Story of the Lady Who Disarmed Two Aggressors With Wit

full_text:
In a turbulent border town of Mesopotamia lived a noble and virtuous matron named Sitt Nur. One afternoon, while her family was working in the olive groves, two armed ruffians broke into her walled garden, seeking to loot the house and intimidate its mistress.

Instead of screaming or showing terror, Sitt Nur stood calmly upon her terrace, greeted them with serene courtesy, and said:
'Welcome, brothers. You enter with drawn daggers, yet you come to a house of peace. If it is gold you seek, sit upon this bench; I shall bring you refreshing mint water and the keys to our grain chest.'

Her absolute composure unnerved the two men. They sat down, glancing at one another in confusion.
Sitt Nur brought them two bowls of water and placed a heavy iron balance upon the table.

'Before you take our grain,' she said with a warm smile, 'resolve a riddle that has divided our village elders. A traveler has two bags: one filled with heavy iron daggers, and the other filled with light silver coins. If he enters a peaceful town, which bag will buy him friends, and which will bring him the gallows?'

The first bandit muttered: 'The silver coins buy friends, of course.'
Sitt Nur replied:
'Then why carry iron daggers when you can earn silver through honest labor?
Look at you: two strong young men, capable of building houses or harvesting dates, choosing to hide in shadows like hunted jackals.
Take these twenty silver dirhams from my household coffer. Go, buy tools, return to your villages with honor, and let no man call you thieves.'

Her profound dignity, gentle reasoning, and moral authority pierced through the crust of their hardened hearts.
The two bandits dropped their heads in shame, sheathed their weapons, and refused to accept the money.
'By Allah, noble lady,' the elder said, 'thy words have slain our wicked intentions more surely than any sword. We came as robbers, but we leave as men who remember our mothers.'

They bowed with deep reverence and departed. They left the border town to find honest labor, proving that moral courage and graceful speech can disarm violence where weapons only breed bloodshed.
moral: Quick intelligence and composed dignity protect the innocent from violence without spilling blood.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Lady With Two Coyntes"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
